battery_monitor.show_item_border_desc: Draw a 1px border around each device tile. Turn off for a borderless look.
battery_monitor.critical_desc: At or below this % uses critical color.
battery_monitor.low_desc: At or below this % uses low color (above critical).
battery_monitor.only_low_desc: Hide devices above the low threshold.
battery_monitor.discovery_mode_desc: Auto scans Home Assistant; manual uses the list below; both merges them.
battery_monitor.include_bin_desc: Maps on = low / off = OK for device_class battery.
battery_monitor.manual_entities_desc: Pick entities to include. Expand a row for overrides.
battery_monitor.exclude_patterns_desc: Entity ids containing these substrings are ignored.
battery_monitor.hidden_entities_desc: Removed from auto-discovery; click × to show again.
battery_monitor.err_empty_desc: Adjust discovery mode, manual entities, or thresholds in the General tab.
battery_monitor.strip_hint: Tap a segment for more-info. Colors reflect battery level.

auto_entity_list.title: Title
auto_entity_list.include_domains_desc: Only entities from these domains (e.g. light, binary_sensor). Empty = all.
auto_entity_list.include_device_classes_desc: Filter by attributes.device_class (e.g. motion, door, temperature).
auto_entity_list.state_filter_desc: Only show entities whose state matches. Leave operator empty to disable.
auto_entity_list.include_keywords_desc: Entity id must contain at least one of these substrings.
auto_entity_list.exclude_keywords_desc: Entity ids containing any of these substrings are ignored.
auto_entity_list.show_unavailable_desc: When off, entities in unavailable or unknown states are hidden.
auto_entity_list.pinned_entities_desc: Always appear first, regardless of filters. Click a chip to edit overrides; hover to remove.
auto_entity_list.hidden_entities_desc: Removed from the auto list. Remove with the × on a chip.
auto_entity_list.entity_desc: Entity to pin to the top.
auto_entity_list.err_empty_desc: Adjust the filters in the General tab or pin some entities.
auto_entity_list.use_entity_color_desc: When an entity exposes a color (light bulb RGB, etc.) use it for the state, icon, and card accent.
auto_entity_list.card_width_desc: Maximum row width in pixels. 0 = fill container.
auto_entity_list.row_gap_desc: Vertical gap between rows. Applies to every style.
auto_entity_list.columns_desc: Arrange rows in a grid. 1 = single column (default).

lunar_phase.pro_description: Lunar Phase is a Pro feature with an animated moon, live lunar data, a month calendar, and a horizon graph.
lunar_phase.config_needed_desc: Choose a location source in the General tab
lunar_phase.location_section_desc: Latitude and longitude used for moon position, rise and set times.
lunar_phase.location_source_desc: Use your Home Assistant location, an entity, or manual coordinates.
lunar_phase.southern_hemisphere_desc: Mirror the moon image the way it appears south of the equator.
lunar_phase.layout_section_desc: Choose the default view, layout style, and moon graphic options.
lunar_phase.default_view_desc: View shown when the card loads.
lunar_phase.layout_desc: Full shows everything; compact styles fit small dashboard slots and expand on tap.
lunar_phase.moon_position_desc: Side of the card the moon graphic sits on (full layout).
lunar_phase.items_per_page_desc: Rows shown before the list paginates. Swipe or use the dots to switch pages.
lunar_phase.show_view_switcher_desc: Header buttons to switch between phase, calendar, and horizon views.
lunar_phase.show_date_nav_desc: Footer with previous / next day arrows and a back-to-today button.
lunar_phase.data_section_desc: Hide individual data rows and control number and time formatting.
lunar_phase.hidden_items_desc: Data rows that should not be displayed.
lunar_phase.number_decimals_desc: Precision for numeric values like illumination and azimuth.
lunar_phase.use_miles_desc: Show the moon distance in miles instead of kilometers.
lunar_phase.time_12hr_desc: Use AM/PM times instead of 24-hour format.
lunar_phase.graph_mode_desc: Today shows midnight to midnight; dynamic shows a rolling 24 hours around now.
lunar_phase.graph_show_time_desc: Time labels at the moonrise and moonset markers.
lunar_phase.graph_show_current_desc: Pulsing marker at the moon's current altitude.
lunar_phase.graph_show_highest_desc: Marker at the moon's transit (highest altitude).
lunar_phase.graph_x_ticks_desc: Hour labels along the bottom of the chart.
lunar_phase.graph_y_ticks_desc: Degree labels along the left of the chart.
lunar_phase.background_style_desc: Backdrop behind the moon and data.
lunar_phase.custom_background_desc: Upload an image or paste a URL.
lunar_phase.show_starfield_desc: Twinkling stars layered over the background.
lunar_phase.show_compact_labels_desc: Show text labels under the compact layout stats.
lunar_phase.header_font_size_desc: Size of the phase name header.
lunar_phase.header_text_transform_desc: Text transform applied to the header.
lunar_phase.header_color_desc: Leave empty for the automatic color.
lunar_phase.label_font_size_desc: Size of data labels and values.
lunar_phase.label_text_transform_desc: Text transform applied to data labels.
lunar_phase.label_color_desc: Leave empty for the automatic color.
lunar_phase.accent_color_desc: Markers, selected days, glow, and pagination. Leave empty for a moonlight silver.

dog_duty.pro_description: Dog Duty is a Pro feature that uses your yard camera and LLM Vision to mark where the dog went, with a scrubber and cleanup tracking.
dog_duty.entities_section_desc: Camera and to-do list that power the Dog Duty map.
dog_duty.camera_desc: Any camera entity (Scrypted, Frigate, native, etc.).
dog_duty.todo_desc: A local to-do list that stores detections. Create one named "Dog Duty" if you do not have it yet.
dog_duty.trigger_desc: Binary sensor from Scrypted/Frigate dog detection or yard motion. Leave blank for manual Scan Now only.
dog_duty.provider_section_desc: Provider config entry used for Scan Now and the generated automation.
dog_duty.provider_desc: Run Check prerequisites in the wizard to refresh the list.
dog_duty.provider_manual_desc: Paste an LLM Vision provider entry_id if it was not auto-detected.
dog_duty.title: Title
dog_duty.show_cleaned_desc: Completed to-do items appear as faded checkmarks.
dog_duty.show_heatmap_desc: Show density overlay of favorite spots in the lookback window.
dog_duty.lookback_desc: How far back the scrubber and markers go.
dog_duty.background_mode_desc: Live camera snapshot or a fixed reference photo of the yard.
dog_duty.reference_image_desc: Upload a still photo of the yard from the same camera angle.
dog_duty.cooldown_desc: Minimum minutes between automation runs / Scan Now calls.
dog_duty.wizard_desc: One-click setup creates a to-do list + automation so scans only run when the dog is outside — no token burn.
dog_duty.wizard_step1_desc: Dog Duty needs the LLM Vision integration (HACS) and at least one AI provider. Local Ollama works for $0.
dog_duty.wizard_step2_desc: Choose your yard camera and Dog Duty to-do list below (Entities section), then continue. Create a Local To-do list named "Dog Duty" in Settings → Devices & services → Helpers if needed.
dog_duty.wizard_step3_desc: Creates an automation that snapshots the camera after dog/motion activity, runs one LLM Vision compare, and writes findings to your to-do list.
dog_duty.wizard_step4_desc: Run an on-demand scan against the current camera frame. Coordinate accuracy is approximate — keep a fixed camera angle.
dog_duty.llm_missing: LLM Vision is not installed. Install it via HACS, add a provider, then check again.
dog_duty.provider_missing: LLM Vision is installed but no providers were detected. Add a provider in the LLM Vision integration.
dog_duty.setup_done: Setup complete. Detections will appear on the map.
dog_duty.todo_manual_hint: Tip: Settings → Devices & services → Helpers → Create Helper → Local To-do → name it "Dog Duty", then pick it in Entities above.
dog_duty.need_provider: Select or paste an LLM Vision provider ID first.
dog_duty.automation_created: Automation created: {id}. Reload automations if it does not appear immediately.
dog_duty.automation_failed: Could not create the automation automatically. You may need admin permissions, or create it manually from the generated template.
dog_duty.test_found: Found {count} spot(s). Markers were added to the to-do list.
dog_duty.test_none: No droppings detected in the current frame.
dog_duty.no_camera: Select a yard camera to show the map
dog_duty.no_events: No detections in this time window
dog_duty.setup_hint: Open the General tab and run the setup wizard to connect a camera, to-do list, and LLM Vision.
dog_duty.setup_guide_title: How to set up LLM Vision
dog_duty.setup_guide_1: Install “LLM Vision” from HACS, then restart Home Assistant.
dog_duty.setup_guide_2: Settings → Devices & services → Add Integration → LLM Vision. On the first Settings screen (timeout / prompts), just press Submit — there is no model to pick here.
dog_duty.setup_guide_3: On the LLM Vision card, press Add Entry (or Configure → Add Entry) and choose a Provider (OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, or Ollama).
dog_duty.setup_guide_4: Use a vision model. Easy picks: gpt-4o-mini (OpenAI), gemini-2.0-flash (Google), or gemma3:12b (Ollama). Text-only models cause “invalid_model”.
dog_duty.setup_guide_5: Come back here and press Check prerequisites.
dog_duty.setup_guide_invalid_model: Seeing “Validation error: invalid_model”? That happens on the Provider screen, not the first Settings screen. Change the Model field to a vision model from the list above (exact spelling), then Submit again.
dog_duty.todo_no_description: This list (e.g. Shopping List) cannot store item descriptions. Markers still work, but a Local To-do named “Dog Duty” is recommended (Settings → Devices & services → Helpers → Local To-do).
dog_duty.detection_section_desc: Tune how Scan Now and the automation look for waste. The AI instructions stay hidden — you only set preferences.
dog_duty.automation_update_hint: Scan Now uses these settings immediately. Re-create the automation below to apply them to automatic scans.
dog_duty.sensitivity_desc: Strict = fewer high-confidence marks. Lenient = more willing to mark uncertain spots.
dog_duty.detect_squatting_desc: Also mark when a dog is clearly squatting or defecating, not only piles on the ground.
dog_duty.min_confidence_desc: Ignore AI spots below this confidence (0–100%).
dog_duty.extra_tips_placeholder: e.g. Our dog is white; piles are usually dark brown near the fence
dog_duty.extra_tips_desc: Tell the AI about your yard. Do not paste long instructions — short notes work best.
dog_duty.example_photos_desc: Up to 3 photos of what waste looks like in your yard. Sent as references with each scan (uses more tokens).
dog_duty.detect_zone_desc: Drag a rectangle on the preview to limit detection to part of the yard (e.g. lawn only).
dog_duty.detect_zone_drag: Drag to draw the detect zone
dog_duty.detect_zone_set: Zone set — outside areas are ignored.
dog_duty.extra_cameras_desc: Optional. Each camera gets its own map; status chips combine across all.
dog_duty.cameras_layout_desc: Stack maps vertically or show them in a grid when you have more than one camera.
dog_duty.scan_mode_section_desc: The mode is chosen automatically from your setup: pick a trigger sensor for the smartest scanning, or let the automation run on a schedule without one.
dog_duty.mode_sensor_desc: A dog / motion sensor starts a scan right after activity ends. Fewest AI calls — recommended if you have one.
dog_duty.mode_scheduled_desc: No sensor needed. The automation scans every {interval} during your active hours. Each scan is one AI call, whether or not the dog was out.
dog_duty.mode_manual_desc: No automation yet. Only the Scan Now button runs a scan — zero background AI cost. Finish the wizard to enable automatic scanning.
dog_duty.scan_interval_desc: How often the automation scans when no trigger sensor is set. Shorter = catches events sooner but uses more AI calls.
dog_duty.active_hours_desc: Scheduled scans only run inside this window, so you are not paying for AI calls while the dog is asleep.
dog_duty.scan_mode_reapply: Changing the trigger sensor or schedule? Re-run "Create automation" in the wizard to update the existing automation.
dog_duty.wizard_mode_sensor: Sensor mode: {sensor} will trigger a scan right after activity ends — the cheapest way to run this.
dog_duty.wizard_mode_scheduled: No trigger sensor selected, so the automation will scan every {interval} between {start} and {end}. That works fine but uses more AI calls — pick a dog/motion sensor in Entities above if you have one.

cleaning_zones.add_first_desc: Open the General tab and add a room with a name and a cleaning interval. A floorplan image is optional — the list works on its own.
cleaning_zones.auto_clean_desc: Optional. When this entity enters the state below, the zone is marked clean automatically — handy for a robot vacuum that reports which room it finished.
cleaning_zones.auto_clean_state_desc: For example “docked” or “returning”. Matching is case-insensitive.
cleaning_zones.default_interval_desc: Used by any zone that has not set its own interval.
cleaning_zones.draw_too_small: That zone was too small — drag out a larger rectangle.
cleaning_zones.floorplan_image_desc: A top-down plan of your home. Any image works — a screenshot of a vacuum map is a good shortcut.
cleaning_zones.floorplan_section_desc: Optional. Without an image the list view still works as a plain room-chore tracker.
cleaning_zones.history_limit_desc: Older entries are deleted so the to-do list does not grow without bound.
cleaning_zones.log_cleaner_desc: Stores a name alongside each entry so you can see who did what.
cleaning_zones.no_zones_editor: No zones yet. Add one below, or drag a rectangle on the floorplan above.
cleaning_zones.overdue_grace_desc: How many days past the interval a room stays merely “due” before it turns overdue.
cleaning_zones.person_entity_desc: Whose name to record. The card cannot tell who tapped it, so this is a fixed attribution.
cleaning_zones.placement_hint: Drag on empty space to draw a new zone. Drag a zone to move it, its bottom-right corner to resize, or the knob above it to rotate. Hold Shift while rotating to snap to 15°.
cleaning_zones.placement_needs_image: Upload a floorplan above to place zones by dragging. You can still add zones and set their position numerically.
cleaning_zones.pro_description: Cleaning Zones is a Pro feature: draw rooms on your floorplan, give each one a cleaning interval, and watch them shade from fresh to overdue. Tap a room to log that it was cleaned.
cleaning_zones.require_confirm_desc: Asks for a second tap. Worth turning on for a wall tablet where stray taps happen.
cleaning_zones.setup_desc: Choose a Local To-do helper under Storage in the General tab. Every clean you log is saved there.
cleaning_zones.show_summary_bar_desc: A one-line count of what needs attention, plus the most overdue room.
cleaning_zones.show_zone_labels_desc: Labels are hidden automatically on zones that are too small to fit them.
cleaning_zones.sort_mode_desc: How rooms are ordered in the list view.
cleaning_zones.staleness_style_desc: How overdue rooms stand out on the map.
cleaning_zones.storage_help: Cleaning history lives on a to-do list so every device in the house sees the same log. Create one under Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → To-do list (Local to-do), name it something like “Cleaning”, then pick it here.
cleaning_zones.title: Title override
cleaning_zones.todo_entity_desc: A Local To-do helper used as storage. Entries are saved as completed items, so they stay out of your active to-do view.
cleaning_zones.todo_no_description: This list cannot store item descriptions (the Shopping List behaves this way). Tracking still works, but the stored data is appended to each item title and looks messy in the Home Assistant to-do panel. A Local To-do helper avoids that.
cleaning_zones.view_mode_desc: What the card shows. Map falls back to the list when no image is set.
cleaning_zones.zone_color_desc: Leave blank to use the fresh → overdue gradient.
cleaning_zones.zone_icon_desc: Shown in the list view and on larger map zones.
cleaning_zones.zone_interval_desc: How often this area should be cleaned.
cleaning_zones.zone_name_desc: What you call this area — “Kitchen”, “Upstairs bathroom”.
cleaning_zones.zone_notes_desc: Optional reminder — “mop, don’t vacuum”, “move the rug”.
cleaning_zones.zone_opacity_desc: How strongly zone tints cover the floorplan.
cleaning_zones.zone_position_desc: Percentages of the image, measured from the top-left corner. Usually easier to set by dragging on the map above.
cleaning_zones.zone_rotation_desc: Angle the zone to line up with a room that is not square to the image, such as on an isometric floorplan.
cleaning_zones.zones_section_desc: One entry per room or area. A name and an interval are all that is required.

battery_fleet.area_filter_desc: Leave empty to include every area. Devices with no area are excluded once a filter is set.
battery_fleet.color_card_bg_desc: Background behind each device row or tile.
battery_fleet.color_critical_desc: Batteries at or below the critical threshold.
battery_fleet.color_low_desc: Batteries at or below the low threshold.
battery_fleet.color_ok_desc: Batteries with nothing to worry about.
battery_fleet.conf_basis: {label} — measured from {hours} h of observed discharge.
battery_fleet.conf_none: Not enough recorded drain yet to make an honest estimate.
battery_fleet.critical_threshold_desc: At or below this percentage a battery is critical.
battery_fleet.devices_section_desc: Auto-discovery finds every battery in Home Assistant with no configuration. Switch to Manual to curate the list yourself.
battery_fleet.discovery_mode_desc: Auto scans Home Assistant, Manual uses only the list below, Both merges them.
battery_fleet.dismiss_auto: Hide this device from the card
battery_fleet.empty_auto_desc: Nothing in Home Assistant reports a battery level. Try enabling battery_level attributes or binary sensors, or relax the exclude patterns.
battery_fleet.empty_manual_desc: Manual discovery is on but the list is empty. Add entities in the General tab, or switch discovery to Auto.
battery_fleet.err_history: Recorder history is unavailable, so levels are shown without predictions.
battery_fleet.error_manual_empty: Add at least one battery entity, or switch discovery to Auto or Both.
battery_fleet.error_thresholds: The critical threshold must be lower than the low threshold.
battery_fleet.exclude_patterns_desc: Any battery whose entity id or name contains one of these words is skipped. Case-insensitive.
battery_fleet.footer_basis: Predictions from {days} days of history · {ready} of {total} devices have enough data
battery_fleet.found_none_desc: Nothing matched. Try turning on battery_level attributes or battery binary sensors below, relax your exclude patterns, or add entities manually.
battery_fleet.group_by_area_desc: Split the list into area headings. Devices with no area are listed last.
battery_fleet.hidden_entities_desc: {count} device(s) dismissed from the card. Remove a chip to bring one back.
battery_fleet.hidden_entities_empty: Nothing dismissed. Use the × on a row in the live preview to hide a device.
battery_fleet.history_days_desc: How far back to read the recorder. Longer windows smooth out noise but cost more to load.
battery_fleet.include_attribute_desc: Picks up vacuums, phones, trackers and other devices that report their battery as an attribute instead of a sensor.
battery_fleet.include_binary_desc: Devices that only report "low" or "OK". They show as 0% or 100% and cannot be predicted.
battery_fleet.layout_desc: Table is the dense planning view, Cards is a tile grid, Compact is one line each.
battery_fleet.low_threshold_desc: At or below this percentage a battery is low. Must be above the critical threshold.
battery_fleet.manual_empty: No manual batteries yet. Add one below.
battery_fleet.manual_heading_desc: Add any entity that reports a battery percentage. Expand a row to set a friendly label, icon and battery type.
battery_fleet.max_items_desc: How many devices to list. The summary bar always counts the whole fleet.
battery_fleet.min_confidence_hours_desc: How many hours of observed draining are required before any estimate is shown. Lower values give faster but shakier predictions.
battery_fleet.predict_replacement_desc: Measure each battery\u2019s drain rate and project when it will need changing.
battery_fleet.prediction_section_desc: Predictions are measured from recorder history, not guessed. A battery needs a day or two of recorded drain before an estimate appears — until then the card honestly says "gathering data".
battery_fleet.pro_description: Battery Fleet reads recorder history to measure how fast every battery in your home is draining, then ranks them by how soon they need replacing.
battery_fleet.replacement_floor_desc: The percentage you consider "dead". Predictions count down to this, not to zero.
battery_fleet.row_battery_type_desc: A note for shopping day, e.g. "CR2032 x2" or "AA x4".
battery_fleet.row_icon_desc: Leave blank to use a battery icon that follows the level.
battery_fleet.row_label_desc: Leave blank to use the entity name.
battery_fleet.show_charging_indicator_desc: Flag rechargeable devices that are charging right now and exclude them from urgency.
battery_fleet.show_drain_rate_desc: Percentage lost per day, measured from history.
battery_fleet.show_eta_desc: The "replace in ~12 days" column. Hidden automatically when there is not enough data.
battery_fleet.show_only_problems_desc: Hide healthy batteries so the card is empty when there is nothing to do.
battery_fleet.show_sparkline_desc: A tiny history graph per device. Skipped when there are too few samples.
battery_fleet.show_summary_bar_desc: The one-line roll-up with counts and the most urgent device.
battery_fleet.sort_mode_desc: Urgency blends the current level with how fast it is falling.
battery_fleet.thresholds_section_desc: Levels at or below these values are coloured and counted as problems.
battery_fleet.title: Title
battery_fleet.title_desc: Header shown above the list. Leave blank for "Battery Fleet".
battery_fleet.urgent_days_desc: A battery projected to die within this many days is flagged urgent and sorted to the top.

plant_care.add_first_desc: Open the General tab and add a plant with a name and a watering interval. Photos and moisture sensors are optional extras.
plant_care.advanced_sensors_desc: If this plant has a moisture probe, the live reading takes over from the schedule guess. Plants without one keep using the schedule.
plant_care.columns_desc: A target, not a hard count — tiles reflow on narrow screens.
plant_care.hemisphere_north: Your Home Assistant location is in the northern hemisphere, so summer peaks in July.
plant_care.hemisphere_south: Your Home Assistant location is in the southern hemisphere, so summer peaks in January.
plant_care.history_limit_desc: Older care entries are removed from the to-do list so it does not grow forever.
plant_care.illuminance_entity_desc: Optional. Shown on the plant detail, not used for scheduling.
plant_care.import_help: Found these plant entities. Importing copies the name and any moisture sensor it could match — you can adjust everything afterwards.
plant_care.import_no_sensor: No moisture sensor matched — schedule only
plant_care.import_none: No plant.* entities found in Home Assistant. Add plants manually instead.
plant_care.import_nothing_new: Everything here has already been imported.
plant_care.layout_desc: Grid for photos, list for density, map to place plants on a floor plan.
plant_care.map_image_desc: Background image for the map layout. Place each plant on it from its row above.
plant_care.map_needed_desc: The map layout needs a background image. Upload one under Layout in the General tab, then place each plant on it.
plant_care.map_place_hint: Every marker is still sitting in the middle. Open a plant in the General tab and click the plan to place it.
plant_care.map_position_help: Click the plan to drop this plant where it lives.
plant_care.map_position_no_image: Upload a floor plan under Layout to place plants by clicking. Until then, use the sliders below.
plant_care.moisture_entity_desc: A sensor reporting soil moisture as a percentage.
plant_care.moisture_source_desc: Plants without a moisture sensor always fall back to the schedule — the card says so on each plant.
plant_care.moisture_threshold_desc: Readings under this percentage mean the plant wants water.
plant_care.no_plants_editor: No plants yet. Add one below, or import the plant entities you already have in Home Assistant.
plant_care.overdue_color_desc: Well past due, or bone dry.
plant_care.overdue_first_desc: Overdue and thirsty plants float to the top instead of keeping your order.
plant_care.plant_fertilize_interval_desc: Set to 0 to turn fertilizing reminders off for this plant.
plant_care.plant_icon_desc: Shown when there is no photo, and as the fallback if a photo fails to load.
plant_care.plant_location_desc: Optional room or spot, shown under the name.
plant_care.plant_name_desc: What you call this plant — “Monstera”, “Kitchen basil”.
plant_care.plant_notes_desc: Optional reminder to yourself — “bottom water only”, “likes it dry”.
plant_care.plant_photo_desc: Optional. A photo makes the grid layout much easier to scan.
plant_care.plant_water_interval_desc: How often this plant wants water.
plant_care.plants_section_desc: Every plant you want to keep an eye on. A watering interval is all that is required — sensors are optional.
plant_care.pro_description: Plant Care is a Pro feature: a visual roster of your houseplants with watering and fertilizing schedules, one-tap care logging, and optional moisture sensors.
plant_care.schedule_section_desc: Used by every plant that does not set its own interval.
plant_care.seasonal_adjust_desc: Stretch watering intervals in winter and shorten them in summer. The change eases across the year rather than flipping at the solstice, and the hemisphere is taken from your Home Assistant location.
plant_care.setup_desc: Choose a Local To-do helper under Storage in the General tab. Watering history is saved there.
plant_care.show_fertilize_desc: Adds a secondary fertilize action for plants that have an interval set.
plant_care.show_photos_desc: Turn off to fall back to icons everywhere.
plant_care.show_summary_bar_desc: A one-line count of thirsty, overdue and happy plants.
plant_care.storage_help: Watering history lives on a to-do list so every device in the house sees the same log. Create one under Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → To-do list (Local to-do), name it something like “Plant Care”, then pick it here.
plant_care.summer_factor_desc: Below 1 waters more often at the height of summer.
plant_care.temperature_entity_desc: Optional. Shown on the plant detail, not used for scheduling.
plant_care.title: Title
plant_care.todo_entity_desc: A Local To-do helper used as storage. Nothing else should write to it.
plant_care.todo_no_description: This list cannot store item descriptions (the Shopping List behaves this way). Care history still works, but the stored data is appended to each item title and looks messy in the Home Assistant to-do panel. A Local To-do helper avoids that.
plant_care.winter_factor_desc: Above 1 stretches the gap between waterings in deep winter.

laundry_tracker.acknowledge_enabled_desc: Adds a button to clear an alert by hand. Resets when the browser reloads.
laundry_tracker.appliance_icon_desc: Leave blank to use the default for this machine type.
laundry_tracker.appliance_kind_desc: Sets the default icon and detection thresholds. Dryers idle higher than washers.
laundry_tracker.appliances_section_desc: Add each machine and point it at a power sensor. A smart plug is enough — no smart appliance required.
laundry_tracker.color_alert_desc: A load is still sitting there.
laundry_tracker.colors_section_desc: Leave any of these blank to follow the Home Assistant theme.
laundry_tracker.display_section_desc: Choose which parts of the card are shown.
laundry_tracker.door_entity_desc: Optional but the most reliable unload signal there is: opening the door after a cycle clears the alert.
laundry_tracker.empty_desc: Open the General tab and point a machine at its power sensor.
laundry_tracker.energy_rate_desc: Cost per kWh used for the cycle cost estimate.
laundry_tracker.est_finish: about {time} left, based on your last {count} cycles
laundry_tracker.est_finish_unknown: not enough past cycles to estimate a finish time yet
laundry_tracker.forgotten_dryer: The dry load is still in the drum.
laundry_tracker.forgotten_washer: The wet load is still in the drum.
laundry_tracker.history_days_desc: Longer windows give better averages but ask more of the recorder.
laundry_tracker.history_error: Could not read recorder history. Live wattage still works.
laundry_tracker.history_section_desc: How far back to read the recorder, and what a kilowatt-hour costs you.
laundry_tracker.layout_desc: Stack the machines vertically, or sit them side by side.
laundry_tracker.learning: Learning your cycles — no completed loads recorded yet.
laundry_tracker.min_cycle_minutes_desc: Shorter runs are treated as noise rather than a real load.
laundry_tracker.no_appliances_hint: No machines yet. Add a washer or a dryer to get started.
laundry_tracker.no_cycles_window: No cycles in the last {days} days
laundry_tracker.no_source: No power or state sensor selected for this machine.
laundry_tracker.notify_message: {name} finished {time} ago and still has a load in it.
laundry_tracker.notify_once_note: Fires at most once per load. A second nag only happens after the next cycle finishes.
laundry_tracker.notify_section_desc: Optional push when a load is left sitting past its grace period.
laundry_tracker.notify_service_desc: For example notify.mobile_app_pixel. Leave blank to turn notifications off.
laundry_tracker.power_entity_desc: Watts reported by a smart plug. This is what cycle detection reads.
laundry_tracker.pro_description: Turn a $15 smart plug into a laundry butler: automatic cycle detection, forgotten-load alerts, and running energy costs.
laundry_tracker.running_states_desc: States of the machine state entity that mean "running". Leave empty for a broad default set.
laundry_tracker.settle_minutes_desc: How long the machine must stay quiet before the cycle closes. Stops a soak pause from ending the wash early.
laundry_tracker.show_energy_desc: Turn off to hide kWh and money figures everywhere on the card.
laundry_tracker.show_handoff_hint_desc: Suggests moving the load when a wash finishes and a dryer is free.
laundry_tracker.show_history_stats_desc: Cycle count, energy, cost and average duration for the window.
laundry_tracker.show_idle_alert_desc: The loud banner when a finished load is still sitting in the machine.
laundry_tracker.show_status_cards_desc: One card per machine with its current phase.
laundry_tracker.show_timeline_desc: A strip of the history window with one lane per machine.
laundry_tracker.show_title_desc: Display a heading above the machines.
laundry_tracker.start_threshold_desc: Watts above which a cycle counts as started.
laundry_tracker.state_entity_desc: Fallback for machines with no power sensor: an entity reporting run/idle from a smart-appliance integration.
laundry_tracker.stats_learning: No completed cycles yet — still learning what your machines look like.
laundry_tracker.stop_threshold_desc: Watts below which the machine looks finished. Keep it under the start threshold.
laundry_tracker.suggested_applied: Applied. Fine-tune them under Advanced detection if a cycle is missed.
laundry_tracker.threshold_helper_desc: What this sensor actually reported over the history window.
laundry_tracker.threshold_loading: Reading recent history for this sensor…
laundry_tracker.threshold_no_data: No recorder history for this sensor yet. Run a load and come back — the defaults will work in the meantime.
laundry_tracker.timeline_empty: No cycles recorded in this window yet.
laundry_tracker.title: Title
laundry_tracker.unload_grace_desc: How long after a cycle ends before the load counts as forgotten.

vehicle_maintenance.battery_entity_desc: Optional. For EVs and plug-in hybrids, shown alongside or instead of fuel.
vehicle_maintenance.colors_section_desc: Leave blank to follow your Home Assistant theme.
vehicle_maintenance.config_needed_desc: Add at least one service interval in the General tab
vehicle_maintenance.currency_symbol_desc: Prefixed to every cost shown on the card.
vehicle_maintenance.delete_log_message: This permanently removes the entry from your service history.
vehicle_maintenance.delete_message: This removes the service and its interval from the card. Entries already written to the service log are kept.
vehicle_maintenance.display_section_desc: Pick a layout and choose which parts of the card are visible.
vehicle_maintenance.distance_unit_desc: Unit used for every interval and reading. Readings from a sensor in the other unit are converted automatically.
vehicle_maintenance.due_soon_days_desc: Remaining days at which a service turns amber.
vehicle_maintenance.due_soon_distance_desc: Remaining distance at which a service turns amber.
vehicle_maintenance.estimated_cost_desc: Used as the default amount when you log this service, and to forecast upcoming spend.
vehicle_maintenance.fuel_entity_desc: Optional. A percentage sensor renders as a bar; anything else is shown as a value.
vehicle_maintenance.hint_no_odometer: Tracking by time only. Add an odometer entity to unlock distance intervals and mileage-stamped log entries.
vehicle_maintenance.hint_odometer_unavailable: The odometer sensor is unavailable, so distance intervals are paused. Time-based tracking is still running.
vehicle_maintenance.interval_distance_desc: How far between services, in {unit}. Use 0 for time-only services like registration.
vehicle_maintenance.interval_months_desc: Months between services. Use 0 for distance-only services like tire rotation.
vehicle_maintenance.last_date_desc: Defaults to the day this service was added, which is only a guess — set your real last service date.
vehicle_maintenance.last_distance_desc: Leave at 0 if you do not know it. Logging a service overwrites this with the reading at the time.
vehicle_maintenance.layout_desc: Hero leads with the vehicle and the next service. List shows every service. Compact is a single summary line.
vehicle_maintenance.log_empty: No services logged yet. Use "Mark serviced" on a service to start your history.
vehicle_maintenance.log_error: Could not read the service log from that to-do list.
vehicle_maintenance.log_limit_desc: How many recent entries the card displays. Older entries stay in the to-do list.
vehicle_maintenance.log_no_storage: Pick a to-do list in the General tab to keep a permanent service history with costs.
vehicle_maintenance.log_write_failed: Could not write to the service log.
vehicle_maintenance.mark_message_no_odometer: Logs {name} as done today. No odometer is configured, so no reading is stored.
vehicle_maintenance.mark_needs_list: Choose a storage list in the General tab to record services from the card
vehicle_maintenance.notes_desc: Part numbers, oil weight, the shop you use.
vehicle_maintenance.odometer_entity_desc: A sensor from your car integration, an OBD dongle, or an input_number you update yourself. Leave blank to track services by time only.
vehicle_maintenance.odometer_none: No odometer selected. Services will be tracked by time only — distance intervals stay dormant until you pick one.
vehicle_maintenance.odometer_offset_desc: Added to every reading, in {unit}. Use this when the sensor was reset or starts from zero — for example a dongle fitted at 82,000 miles.
vehicle_maintenance.odometer_unit_assumed: no unit on the sensor, assuming {unit}
vehicle_maintenance.odometer_unreadable: That entity is not reporting a number right now. Distance tracking stays off until it does; time intervals keep working.
vehicle_maintenance.presets_hint: Typical intervals you can adjust after adding. Distances are converted when your unit is kilometers.
vehicle_maintenance.pro_description: Track oil changes, tire rotations and registration by distance or time — whichever comes first — with a cost-tracked service log built from your car\u2019s odometer.
vehicle_maintenance.projection: About {days} days away at {perDay} per day, based on {window} days of history.
vehicle_maintenance.row_from_log: Tracking from the service log: last done {detail}. This overrides the two fields above.
vehicle_maintenance.services_empty: No services yet. Add one below, or start from a preset.
vehicle_maintenance.services_section_desc: Each service is due on whichever comes first: distance or time. Set an interval to 0 to switch that axis off.
vehicle_maintenance.show_costs_desc: Adds amounts to log entries plus a total spend figure.
vehicle_maintenance.storage_section_desc: Service history is stored in a Home Assistant to-do list so it survives restarts and syncs to every device.
vehicle_maintenance.thresholds_section_desc: When a service starts warning, and how much history to show. The defaults suit most vehicles.
vehicle_maintenance.title: Title override
vehicle_maintenance.title_desc: Leave blank to use the vehicle name.
vehicle_maintenance.todo_entity_desc: Create a Local To-do helper under Settings \u2192 Devices & services \u2192 Helpers \u2192 To-do list, then pick it here.
vehicle_maintenance.todo_missing: Without a list, service history is not retained. Interval tracking still works from the last-service values on each service below.
vehicle_maintenance.todo_no_description: This list cannot store item descriptions (Shopping List behaves this way). Logging still works, but the stored data rides along in the item title and looks messy in the Home Assistant to-do UI. A Local To-do helper is recommended.
vehicle_maintenance.unit_offer: Unit changed to {unit}. Your interval numbers were left exactly as they were. Convert them?
vehicle_maintenance.vehicle_image_desc: Optional. Used as the hero banner; a clean icon header is shown when empty.
vehicle_maintenance.vehicle_name_desc: Shown as the heading in the hero layout.
vehicle_maintenance.vehicle_section_desc: Name your vehicle and point the module at its odometer. Everything else is optional.

vampire_power.analysis_section_desc: A device is measured by the wattage it never drops below. A longer window gives a steadier estimate but takes longer to load.
vampire_power.baseline_percentile_desc: Which point of the wattage distribution counts as idle. 0.10 means the level the device stayed at or below for 10% of the window. Lower is stricter and reports a lower floor; higher includes light activity.
vampire_power.cost_period_desc: Annual figures are the ones large enough to act on; daily figures are easier to sanity-check.
vampire_power.cost_section_desc: What the wasted energy is worth. Costs are estimates based on a flat rate.
vampire_power.currency_symbol_desc: Shown in front of every cost figure.
vampire_power.discovery_mode_desc: Auto scans Home Assistant for power sensors, Manual uses only the list below, Both merges them.
vampire_power.dismissed_desc: {count} devices were dismissed from the card and are excluded from the ranking and the totals.
vampire_power.dismissed_empty: Nothing dismissed. Use the × on a row in the card preview to hide a device you do not want ranked.
vampire_power.energy_rate_desc: Cost of one kilowatt-hour, taken from your electricity bill.
vampire_power.entities_desc: Sensors added here are always analyzed, even when the whole-home filter would have skipped them.
vampire_power.err_empty_desc: This module needs sensors that report watts — smart plugs or an energy monitor. Add one under Sensors in the General tab.
vampire_power.err_history_desc: The recorder did not return data for these sensors. Check that the recorder integration is keeping history for them.
vampire_power.error_manual_empty: Add at least one power sensor, or switch discovery to Auto or Both.
vampire_power.error_range: The standby noise floor must be lower than the always-on cutoff.
vampire_power.exclude_patterns_desc: Sensors whose entity id or name contains any of these words are skipped. Auto discovery already skips whole-home meters (names like total, house, grid or mains); add your own words here for anything else you never want ranked.
vampire_power.found_capped: Only the first {max} are analyzed to keep the recorder query fast.
vampire_power.found_none_hint: Smart plugs and energy monitors expose these. Switch to Manual to add one by hand.
vampire_power.found_ok_hint: Whole-home and grid meters are skipped so they cannot swamp the ranking.
vampire_power.highlight_threshold_desc: Devices idling at or above this wattage are drawn in the offender colour.
vampire_power.hint_many: The top {count} devices cost {cost} a year while idle. Switching them off on a schedule would recover most of that.
vampire_power.hint_one: {name} alone costs {cost} a year doing nothing. A scheduled smart plug would recover most of that.
vampire_power.history_days_desc: How far back to read the recorder. Seven days covers a full weekly routine; longer windows need recorder history to match.
vampire_power.layout_desc: Ranked shows a bar per device, Cards is a tile grid, Compact is a dense list.
vampire_power.loading_note: Analyzing {count} power sensors over {days} days of history…
vampire_power.max_items_desc: The total bar always covers every analyzed device, even when the list is trimmed.
vampire_power.max_standby_watts_desc: Floors above this belong to genuinely always-on appliances such as a fridge or a server. They are listed separately instead of being ranked as standby waste.
vampire_power.min_standby_watts_desc: Standby loads under this are treated as measurement noise and left out entirely.
vampire_power.no_waste_desc: Every sensor idled below {watts} W across the last {days} days. Lower the noise floor under Analysis to see smaller loads.
vampire_power.note_always_on: {count} always-on devices draw more than {watts} W even at rest ({names}). They are running, not idling.
vampire_power.note_capped: Analyzing the first {analyzed} of {total} power sensors.
vampire_power.note_insufficient: {count} sensors need more history before they can be ranked.
vampire_power.pro_description: Vampire Power reads your recorder history to find the standby loads that never switch off, and tells you what each one costs per year.
vampire_power.sensors_section_desc: Choose which power sensors are analyzed. Auto finds every sensor reporting watts, so most homes need nothing here.
vampire_power.show_bars_desc: Each row gets a bar sized against the worst offender.
vampire_power.show_cost_desc: Turn off to show wattage only.
vampire_power.show_savings_hint_desc: A one-line summary of what the worst offenders add up to.
vampire_power.show_title_desc: Display a header above the card.
vampire_power.show_total_bar_desc: The headline figure for the whole home.
vampire_power.sort_mode_desc: Cost ranks by annual waste and breaks ties in favour of devices that are almost purely idle.
vampire_power.title: Title
vampire_power.title_desc: Leave blank to use the module name.
vampire_power.total_footer: Across {devices} devices, measured over {days} days of history

my_presets.empty_message: Share a layout from the card editor to submit your first preset.
my_presets.confirm_withdraw: Withdraw this pending submission or revision?
my_presets.confirm_delete: Delete this preset? This cannot be undone.
